candidates.buyer: Small shops, takeaways, bars and food vendors; family firms in Apia and Savai'i
candidates.existing: No vendor seen. Application forms and licences are paper-based; the trade portal at samoa.tradeportal.org lists the procedures but I did not confirm whether it takes online applications.
candidates.name: Licence-renewal compliance calendar for shops, takeaways and bars (business licence + alcohol licence + food health certificate + food handler cards)
candidates.trigger: Business Licences Act 1998 (no trading without a current licence; Register under s9). Alcohol Control Act 2020 renewal on the same cycle (2023 deadline 31 March, non-renewal means revocation). Food Act 2015 s13 health certificate attached to the licence application. Food handler health cards.
candidates.trigger_note: Per-licence renewals cluster each year, so a reminder and document-pack service is plausible but thin.
candidates.unchecked: Competitor search in Samoan (e.g. software or app plus laisene pisinisi plus fa'amanuiaga) was not run because the search budget was used up. Not checked: number of licensed shops and bars, whether MCR has an online renewal portal, fee levels, and whether anyone would pay for a reminder service. Market is very small.

candidates.buyer: Bus and taxi owners (reserved to Samoan citizens under the Foreign Investment Act 2000)
candidates.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, small bus fleets
candidates.existing: None seen. Competitor search not run.
candidates.name: Bus and taxi owner fleet compliance: quarterly or twice-yearly LTA Certificate of Fitness reminders, late-fee avoidance, document pack
candidates.trigger: LTA: taxis renew March and September, commercial buses every 3 months; Certificate of Fitness plus Business Licence Certificate and commercial driver's licence; late inspection fee SAT 53 (taxi) and SAT 26.50 (bus); offence to drive a PSV with an expired certificate.
candidates.unchecked: Number of PSV operators and fleet sizes; whether LTA already sends reminders; current fee schedule; the 2018 taxi age rule. The 2019 quarterly audit report may be stale. Low value per customer.

candidates.buyer: Foreign investors, trustees and local firms with foreign shareholders; Samoan shop owners at risk of reserved-activity breaches
candidates.category: 33. Foreign Investment Act reserved activities and Amendment Bill 2026
candidates.evidence: https://samoaobserver.ws/category/samoa/121615 ; https://www.mcil.gov.ws/ (May 2024 MCIL notice reported via search: 140 of 300 shop renewals in 2023 suspected foreign-run)
candidates.name: Foreign Investment Amendment Bill 2026: registration certificate (24-month renewal) and beneficial owner disclosure tooling
candidates.trigger: Bill passed second reading in August 2026 and is with the Economic Committee, so not law. Would add certificates valid 24 months, beneficial-owner disclosure for companies and trusts, trustees reporting changes within 14 working days, fines up to 500 penalty units. Section 14 of the 2000 Act already makes reserved-activity breaches an offence.
candidates.unchecked: Whether the Bill becomes law and when; whether existing businesses must re-register; population is mostly law-firm and corporate-agent work, not quiet family firms.

coverage.found: LTA requires taxis to renew twice a year (March and September) and commercial buses four times a year, with a Certificate of Fitness. coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Not searched (budget).

coverage.found: Not searched (budget). Only the RSE and PALM recruiter regime was seen, under category 15.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (consolidated 2025). The Central Bank of Samoa and the Samoa FIU publish guides for lawyers, accountants and real estate agents covering customer identification, record keeping, transaction reporting and a compliance regime. Small population of reporters. Candidate C8.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Tourism Development Act 2012 licenses all accommodation, including beach fales and homestays; the Samoa Tourism Authority is the regulator. About 128 properties as of 2020. No guest register or levy rule found. Candidate C7.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: MAF Biosecurity export licence per destination, registered farm sourcing and phytosanitary certification. Fisheries Management (Fish Processing and Export) Regulations 2022 cover processing licences and export certification. Candidates C4 and C6.

coverage.category: 31. Alcohol licensing (Alcohol Control Act 2020, Alcohol Control Board)
coverage.found: The Act commenced 1 July 2021 and replaced the Liquor Act 2011. Licences are renewed annually on the business licence cycle; in 2023 the deadline was extended to 31 March and non-renewal meant revocation. Applications are paper forms from the Liquor Board secretary. Candidate C1.

coverage.category: 32. Food Act 2015 health certificates and food handler cards
coverage.found: Health certificate from the Director General of Health, issued by the Food Safety Office at Motootua, and required before a food business licence. Food handlers need a health card (SAT 10), training and medical screening. Candidate C1.

coverage.found: The Bill passed second reading in August 2026 and went to the Economic Committee; it is not law yet. It would add a registration certificate (24 months, renewable) and beneficial owner disclosure, with trustees reporting changes within 14 working days. In 2023, 140 of 300 shop renewals were suspected of being foreign-run. Candidate C3.

coverage.category: 34. Business Licences Act 1998 annual renewals and the Register of Business Licences (Ministry of Customs and Revenue)
coverage.found: No one may carry on business without a current licence; the Register is kept under section 9. Renewal now includes beneficial-owner checks. Renewal is a precondition for the LTA, alcohol and food licences. Candidate C1.

coverage.category: 35. Tobacco Control Act 2008 and Licensing Regulations 2020
coverage.found: Licences apply to manufacturers, importers, distributors, hotel owners and nightclub owners only; no shop licence found. Very few licensees. Nothing worth building.

coverage.category: 36. Fisheries and Shipping Acts: vessel licensing, fish processing and export
coverage.found: Fisheries Act 1988 (local commercial vessel licensing, Part VA processing and marketing), the 2022 Processing and Export Regulations, and Shipping Act 1998 vessel registration. Exempt-vessel list and small-boat rules not read. Candidate C4.

coverage.category: 37. Money transfer operators and exchange control (Central Bank of Samoa)
coverage.found: 11 licensed MTOs and money changers in the 2026 Exchange Control Booklet, with delegated approval limits (SAT 50,000 for local investment transfers from August 2023). MTOs handle about 80% of remittance inflows. Candidate C10.

coverage.category: 38. Companies Act 2001 annual returns (Registry of Companies, MCIL)
coverage.found: MCIL notice of 3 June 2026: every company files an annual return in its anniversary month, and non-filers can be removed after six months. The portal at businessregistries.gov.ws emails reminders and has no financial statements requirement. Candidate C9.

coverage.found: Ministry notice of 1 April 2026: mandatory refresher training 30 April to 7 May 2026, no more extensions, penalties to begin. Already known as K01 and K02.

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Labour and Employment Relations Act 2013 has s37 (contracts of service for domestic workers) and s32 minimum wages; MCIL 2025 employer guideline defines a domestic worker as working in a private dwelling house, and there is a 2025 Employment Agreement Form (amended July 2025). The Act 2023 amendment applies alongside it. SNPF applies to employers with one or more employees (third-party payroll guides; rates disagree between sources). Could not read s37 text, the guideline (404) or confirm whether private households must register with SNPF or lodge agreements. Nothing new beyond generic payroll, which is out of scope. Households number few in a market this small.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No dealer licensing or record-keeping regime found; only NZ results came back. Samoa Observer 2016: two exporters (Pacific Recycle, Waste Management) collect scrap from hotels, schools and villages, exports stalled on price. UN COMTRADE via Trading Economics shows small ferrous scrap exports in 2024 (about US$173k to Bangladesh). No MNRE permit regime found. Very few operators.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No Samoa second-hand dealer or pawnbroker statute surfaced; every result was NZ Secondhand Dealers and Pawnbrokers Act 2004. Not confirmed that none exists (PacLII was not searched directly). Nothing new beyond K03-type items; no candidate.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No dismantler or used-parts licence found. Vehicle import age cap is 8 years from manufacture per recent news (older rule 10 years; date unconfirmed). Islands Business reports growing 'vehicle graveyards' and no end-of-life vehicle policy or law. MCIL published a national used-vehicle consumer standard. Nothing to build for.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No beekeeper or apiary registration found. MAF (July 2026) reaffirms the ban on imported honey and bee products under the Bee and Bee Products Prohibition Order 1999 and the Quarantine (Biosecurity) Act 2005. Only about 41 active beekeepers (UNDP, 2021); 21 beekeepers and 403 hives in 2012 PHAMA survey. Too few to sell to.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Water Resources Management Act 2008 Part V s12 requires licences and permits to drill for water or abstract it; MNRE administers; review process s13 and offences s15. Forms, fees, driller count and any reporting duty unconfirmed. Few drillers; government-run licensing of a tiny group.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Occupational Safety and Health Act 2002 plus OSH Regulations 2017, administered by MCIL. Could not retrieve text (PacLII fetch 403) or confirm any plant registration or periodic inspection certificate regime. Few lifts in the country. No candidate.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Water Schemes Act 2015 (assent 2 Sept 2015, in force 3 Sept 2018) recognises Independent Water Schemes as the second water service provider after Samoa Water Authority; community water committees under s7 keep funds and accounts, set fees, and an Independent Water Schemes Association exists (s16). About 32 villages manage water by committee in one thesis. Committee duties include fee proposals and accounts, but no external filing duty verified. Weak lead, logged as a candidate.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Pesticides Regulations 2011 (S.R. 2011/27): no one may import, store, sell, distribute, apply or use a pesticide unless it is registered and the person holds a Pesticide Dealer's licence; Pesticides Technical Committee decides, Registrar enforces; registration fee T345 per item, annual licence T230 per item; applications at the Quarantine Wharf Office, Matautu. Premises inspected before licence (box or room for storage). 2020 Samoa Observer found paraquat sold without checking user licences. Register and sales-record duties not confirmed (regulation text was not fetchable). Small group of retailers.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Burials Ordinance 1961: residents must be buried in a registered village cemetery or Government cemetery; cemeteries must be fenced; Minister may permit other disposal. Repatriation of bodies under the Human Remains Repatriation Policy 2016 (MPMC) with Ministry of Health clearance. No funeral director licensing or burial permit regime found. Burial is mostly family and village land; no candidate.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Co-operatives under the Co-operative Societies Ordinance 1952 (registrar is MCIL CEO); credit unions under the Credit Unions Act 2015 (MCIL registrar; MCIL page still cites 1960 Ordinance). MCIL public notice dated 31 Aug 2026 lists 40 co-operative societies (register numbers 458 to 1130) that must contact the Registry before 1 Oct 2026 or be de-registered. Shows a neglected register but the duty is on dormant bodies, not a recurring workflow. Annual return and audit duties not confirmed. Co-op and society registers are not online. Logged a weak candidate.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: No private security licensing statute found for Samoa (Tonga, Fiji and PNG have one; Samoa seems not to). No labour-hire or manpower agency licence found; MCIL has exclusive right to run RSE and PALM, so overseas recruitment is state-run. Employment permits for non-citizens through MCIL. Companies must file an annual return in their anniversary month (MCIL reminder, June 2026). Nothing new.

result.reason: The duty is real. The Business Licences Act 1998 sets licence renewal (s14 per a search summary, not checked in the Act text). The Alcohol Control Act 2020 has a renewal section (s29), and in 2023 non-renewal meant revocation of the alcohol licence. A Nov 2025 government statement allowed early renewal (Nov 2025 to Jan 2026) and said online submission options exist. The MCIL portal businessregistries.gov.ws covers company filings, FICs and PPS, and no source I found lists licence renewal there. No third-party reminder or compliance software was found, but I ran no Samoan-language vendor search beyond one. The market is tiny and the renewal is annual and widely known. Buyers are scattered, a reminder is low value, and willingness to pay is weak. I could not confirm the fee: the 2024 brochure reportedly says SAT$640, which is unchecked. I found no count of licensed shops or bars.

The duty is real. Produce must come from a MAF-registered farm, commercial exporters need a licence per destination, and goods need treatment, inspection and a phytosanitary certificate (A1 poster, MAF Biosecurity page, PHAMA taro manual). The Quarantine (Biosecurity) Act 2005 lets the Minister ban exports. I found no private software for it. Weaknesses: the market is tiny, probably dozens of active exporters. Donor-funded PHAMA Plus and MAF's ePhyto/SQID work (2017-19) could cover the certificate step. Kava and nonu rules were not found. Penalties and the exporter count were not found. Willingness to pay is low and the process is mostly one-off certificates, so recurrence is weak.
